title: Shreyas Iyer Is India's New T20I Captain. Suryakumar Yadav Has Been Dropped Entirely.
excerpt: The selectors did not ease SKY out. They left him out of both squads. Iyer, who last played a T20I in 2023, will lead India through the 2028 World Cup cycle.
body:
Shreyas Iyer's phone rang on Saturday evening. On the other end was Ajit Agarkar, the chairman of selectors, with the news every cricketer dreams of hearing: he would captain India in T20 internationals.

The 31-year-old Mumbai batter replaces Suryakumar Yadav, who led India to their third T20 World Cup title earlier this year but has been dropped from the squad entirely following an extended slump in form. It is a sharp, decisive turn in India's white-ball setup — and, for Indian cricket fans in the diaspora, a reminder that the sport's most powerful board never stands still for long.

## The Case Against Suryakumar

Suryakumar Yadav's numbers tell their own story. In the 2026 T20 World Cup, he managed just 242 runs from nine matches at a strike rate of 136.72, with only one significant innings — an unbeaten 84 against the United States. The IPL 2026 season offered no relief: 270 runs in 13 matches at an average of 20.77 for Mumbai Indians. For a player who redefined modern T20I batting with his 360-degree strokeplay, the decline was impossible to ignore.

The selectors decided not to ease him out gradually. He has not simply lost the captaincy — he has been left out of both the Ireland and England squads altogether. "It was a difficult call," Agarkar acknowledged at the press conference, but offered no ambiguity: Suryakumar would need to find form in domestic cricket before coming back into the reckoning.

## Why Iyer

Shreyas Iyer's credentials for the job were hiding in plain sight. He captained Kolkata Knight Riders to their third IPL title in 2024, the franchise's most dominant campaign in years. Released by KKR despite that success, he was signed by Punjab Kings for ₹26.75 crore and promptly led them to the 2025 final.

His franchise leadership record speaks directly to the selectors' reasoning. "Led a team to an IPL title. His own performances have been good. He was close to being part of the World Cup squad. In my opinion, a standout candidate," Agarkar said.

Iyer last played a T20I in December 2023, against Australia. The 30-month gap is unusual for a new captain, but the selectors appear to be betting on his maturity, his middle-order anchor role, and his established relationships with coach Gautam Gambhir. The two have history: Gambhir made Iyer captain of Delhi Capitals back in 2018, and was the mentor when KKR won the title under Iyer in 2024.

## The Road Ahead

Iyer's first assignment begins on June 26 with a two-match T20I series against Ireland in Belfast, followed by a five-match T20I series against England in July. He has also been named in the squad for the Asian Games in Japan later this year. The appointment is clearly long-term: Iyer is expected to lead India through to the 2028 T20 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand.

## Sooryavanshi and Bumrah: The Subplots

The squad announcement carried two other significant decisions. Fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, fresh off an IPL 2026 campaign where he topped the run charts with 776 runs and broke Chris Gayle's all-time sixes record, received his maiden India call-up. If he debuts, he will become the youngest player to represent India's men's senior team, surpassing Sachin Tendulkar's record.

Jasprit Bumrah has been rested for both T20I tours as part of India's workload management strategy. However, the fast bowler has been named in the Asian Games squad, signalling that the BCCI views the continental event — where cricket will be played for the first time since 2014 — with real seriousness.

## What NRIs Should Know

For Indian cricket fans in the United States and United Kingdom, these tours offer prime viewing opportunities. The Ireland series in Belfast and the England series across multiple English venues will be accessible across time zones, and the diaspora's emotional investment in a fresh captaincy era — combined with the debut of a teenage prodigy — makes this one of the most anticipated bilateral stretches in recent memory.

India's T20I squad: Shreyas Iyer (captain), Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Sanju Samson (wk), Tilak Varma, Hardik Pandya, Rinku Singh, Washington Sundar, Ravi Bishnoi, Arshdeep Singh, Mohammed Siraj, Dhruv Jurel, Ramandeep Singh, Harshit Rana, Mayank Yadav.
